title: Wendell and the Regiment
premise: In 1847, Noor Thornbury — a pearl diver's child indentured to the Halvard Trading Company on a frozen northern river — has survived seven years by knowing when to be silent. When a sealed letter arrives naming the Thornbury family as conspirators in a scheme to corner the season's entire pearl trade, Noor discovers their late mother was no diver at all but the estranged heir of the company's founder. As the river ice thaws and only one berth remains on the last ship out, Noor must decide which family member escapes the coming reckoning: the brother who betrayed them, the aunt who raised them, or themselves. In the end, Noor gives up the berth, exposes the plot using their mother's hidden ledger, and chooses love over inheritance — staying to rebuild the company honestly rather than flee it.
about_author: V. M. Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the nineteenth century before turning to fiction. They write historical fiction about people history recorded only in margins and footnotes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A day in the life of an indentured clerk-diver at Halvard's river station: weighing pearls, recording silences, avoiding the overseer's questions about family. Establishes the rules Noor lives by. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a loneliness Noor refuses to name.

chapters.title: A Letter Under Seal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter addressed to 'the Thornbury heirs' — a name Noor hasn't used in seven years. The letter names the family in a conspiracy to defraud the company. Noor burns it, then can't stop thinking about it. Beat: dread arriving like weather.

chapters.title: Brother of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor tracks down Elias, the older brother who sold them into indenture, now a company factor. He admits receiving his own letter and hints he's already made arrangements. Beat: old wounds reopened; Noor realizes Elias may be guilty of more than abandonment.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Searching their mother's few effects, Noor finds a false bottom in her diving chest containing a ledger in fine handwriting — accounts that don't match any company book. Beat: the first crack in everything Noor believed about their origins.

chapters.title: The Founder's Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Aunt Sefi. Sefi reveals in fragments that their mother was Marguerite Halvard, the founder's disowned daughter, and the ledger proves she was cheated of her inheritance. Beat: grief braided with fury; the past stops being past.

chapters.title: Ice Season Rules
chapters.summary: Company steward Brandt's POV. Brandt learns of the letters and begins quietly investigating the Thornburys, motivated less by loyalty than by his own debts. Beat: menace without violence; the machinery of power starts to turn.

chapters.title: The Diver's Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor approaches Master Halvard's granddaughter Imogen, who runs the pearl house, offering information in exchange for protection. Their alliance sparks something neither expected. Beat: cautious warmth; two people recognizing each other across class lines.

chapters.title: Elias Signs
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Pressed by Brandt, Elias signs testimony implicating the whole family in exchange for passage on the spring ship. He tells himself it's survival. Beat: self-justification curdling into shame.

chapters.title: Night on the Weighing Floor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor and Imogen compare the mother's ledger against the company books and find systematic theft — someone inside has been skimming for years under the family's name. Beat: intimacy forged in lamplight and numbers.

chapters.title: Sefi Refuses the Ship
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Noor offers Sefi the single berth they've secured; Sefi refuses, insisting the young deserve the escape. Beat: stubborn love; the theme of sacrifice made explicit for the first time.

chapters.title: Brandt's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt realizes the true thief is his own superior, but exposing it would ruin him too. He decides to let the Thornburys hang instead. Beat: corruption choosing convenience over conscience.

chapters.title: The River Opens Early
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Unseasonable warmth means the ice will break weeks early — the last ship's berth becomes truly final. Noor must choose who sails: Elias, Sefi, or themselves. Beat: pressure tightening like a band around the chest.

chapters.title: Confession at the Pearl House
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen confesses her grandfather's role in disinheriting Marguerite and offers Noor the company archive. She asks Noor to stay and fight, not flee. Beat: love offered openly, duty pulling the other way.

chapters.title: Elias Comes Back
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Drunk and terrified, Elias begs Noor to take the berth, revealing Brandt coerced his testimony. Noor sees the boy who once protected them beneath the man who sold them. Beat: forgiveness considered, not yet granted.

chapters.title: The Berth Decision
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The chapter of choice: Noor walks the frozen dock through every option and finally signs the berth over to Elias — not as absolution, but because someone must live to tell the truth. Beat: quiet devastation; love against duty resolved one way.

chapters.title: Arrest at Dawn
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Company agents arrest Sefi and Noor for fraud on the eve of sailing. Brandt watches, complicit, as the frame closes. Beat: betrayal at its coldest; hope at its lowest.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Before the company tribunal, Noor produces the mother's ledger and reads the true accounts aloud, naming the real thief — the director above Brandt. Beat: the silenced voice finally speaking; the room tilting.

chapters.title: Imogen Stands
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen publicly backs Noor, risking her name and inheritance, and forces the tribunal to audit the books. Beat: courage as contagion; love choosing sides in daylight.

chapters.title: What the Ice Gives Up
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The river breaks; the ship leaves with Elias aboard. The director is exposed, Brandt turns state's evidence to save himself, and Sefi is freed. Beat: release after suffocation; justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV. Legally restored to Marguerite's claim, the family holds shares in Halvard's — and Sefi hands the decision of what to do with them to Noor. Beat: power offered where power once wounded.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A new ship, new season, and a berth with Noor's name on it — passage south, away from everything. Noor stands at the gangplank beside Imogen and lets it sail empty. Beat: the choice made visible; staying as an act of love.

chapters.title: First Pearls of the Season
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, epilogue. Months later, Noor co-manages the reformed pearl house, teaching new indentured children to read their own contracts. A letter arrives from Elias in the south. Beat: earned peace; inheritance reclaimed as responsibility, not possession.
